the proposed method of simultaneous extraction of neutral monos accharides and pectin from sugar beet pulp is an effective and environmentally friendly process, with the potential to be implemented on an industrial scale.

the proposed one step process of hydrothermal extraction of waste sugar beet pulp leads to effective simultaneous production of pectins and neutral monosacharides with a relatively hight yield and satisfactory purity, without presence of an acidic catalist.

the optimization of the simultaneous hydrothermal extraction of pectin with the co production of neutral monosaccarides from waste biomass from sugar refining.
the optimization of the yield of pectorins and monosaccharide from sugar beet pulp.

the development of an environmentally friendly, simple and effective method for the hydrothermal extraction of pectin, neutral monosacharides and other valuable components from sugar beet pulp, which is a waste product from sugar refining.

a new method for the simultaneous hydrothermal extraction of pectin with neutral monosacharides has been developed, which is environmentally friendly, simple and effective, and can be used to treat waste product from the industry.
the proposed method is a promising alternative for the production of pectic polysaccharides, neutral monosacchrides, and their co production.
the Doehlert design methodology is very effective and efficient for the modelling of the hydrothermal extraction process of pectin from waste sugar beet pulp.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new, environmentally sound and effective process, which is based on a one stage hydrothermally assisted extraction of waste product from the refining of sugar beet pulp, and that this process may be implemented in an industrial environment.
the hydrothermal extraction of waste biomass is an effective way to co produce pectin and monosaccharide from waste biomass of sugar refining.
the hydrothermal extraction of pectin from sugar beet pulp is a promising technology, which can be used as an effective method for the production of neutral monosacharides and pectin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydrothermal process can be a good substitute for the currently used chemical process.
a single stage process for simultaneous production of pectins and neutral monoscahrides can be used for treatment of waste biomass from sugar refining.

a one step hydrothermal extraction of pectin from sugar beet pulp can be successfully used as a simple, effective, and economically viable process for the production of pectic material and neutral monosacharides.
